items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: hang out with Don, who taught me a lot. Menza taught me a lot. I mean he was like a father to me

ctx.x: Were those guys, did they teach you anything?

Yeah I mean Al Porcino and Art Pepper came on right at the same time, right? So I sat next to Art Pepper for almost a year on Buddy’s band, and Menza came on around the same time too. See when Jay Corre left in Vegas in ’68 I took the tenor chair for about a month and then Don Menza came on the lead chair and I went back to the fourth chair, which was good for me because I got a chance to kind of hang out with Art Pepper and hang out with Don, who taught me a lot. Menza taught me a lot. I mean he was like a…
Yeah. I heard a story, something about the Playboy Club with Buddy Rich and Al?

items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: He had upstate people too. Joe Romano, Pat LaBarbera, Sal—

ctx.x: Well the people that put him down are the people that were mediocre and that couldn’t play. And they hated him. I think it’s very simple. I mean you talk to Sweets Edison about Buddy and he says, “Oh man,” he gets like rekindled. You’d get ready to play, and Buddy’d be there and he’d be propelling you along, making it easier for you to play.
He had upstate people too. Joe Romano, Pat LaBarbera, Sal—
